The image displays mature, dry soybean stems after harvest. One stem in the center has a distinct gray/black speckled appearance. This pattern is consistent with the description of Charcoal Rot, which mentions "fungal structures called microsclerotia fill root and stem tissues... characteristic charcoal-sprinkled appearance develops on roots and stems." The tiny black specks visible on the stem are a key diagnostic feature of Charcoal Rot. While other diseases cause stem discoloration, the "charcoal-sprinkled" look is unique to this pathogen.
